title: Air Quality Alert
location: Clackamas, OR; Marion, OR; Multnomah, OR

details.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory, which is IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 PM PDT THIS EVENING.

An Air Quality Advisory for Smoke and Ozone remains in effect.
Wildfires burning in the region combined with forecasted conditions
will cause air quality to reach unhealthy levels due to smoke and
ozone at times through 6 PM today.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

More information about air quality can be found at:
www.orcaa.org
www.swcleanair.gov
www.oregon.gov/DEQ
www.lrapa.org

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

title: Flood Warning
location: Harrison, WV

details.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in West
Virginia...

West Fork River above Clarksburg affecting Harrison County.

For the West Fork River...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...West Fork River above Clarksburg.

* WHEN...Until Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Water begins to enter some homes along the
low sections near the river. Liberty Avenue floods. At 15.0 feet,
Homes along the low sections of the river on Liberty Avenue and
Route 19 flood. At 16.0 feet, Areas of Baltimore Street and River
Road flood. At 18.0 feet, Major flooding occurs along the river in
Clarksburg.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:15 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:15 PM EDT Wednesday was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet this afternoon. It
will then fall below flood stage just after midnight tonight to
5.0 feet early Friday morning and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 18.1
feet on 12/09/1978.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/rlx.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 100 AM EDT.

title: Extreme Heat Warning
location: Fannin; Lamar; Delta

details.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with heat index values up to 113.

* WHERE...Fannin, Delta, and Lamar Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events.
details.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

Extreme heat is dangerous, especially for those without reliable
shelter. Limit time outdoors during the hottest time of the day,
typically from 2 to 7 PM, rest in the shade when possible, and drink
plenty of water. Locate nearby cooling centers through local
resources or dial 2-1-1 in Texas.

activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

Extreme heat is dangerous, especially for those without reliable
shelter. Limit time outdoors during the hottest time of the day,
typically from 2 to 7 PM, rest in the shade when possible, and drink
plenty of water. Locate nearby cooling centers through local
resources or dial 2-1-1 in Texas.

details.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Frio River At Tilden affecting Live Oak and McMullen Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Frio River at Tilden.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 29.8 feet, Major flooding occurs. Disastrous flooding
of commercial and residential buildings in Tilden. Restuarant on
the right bank of the Frio River had 3 to 4 feet of water in it.

- At 11:15 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 24.3 feet.

- The latest USGS measurement of the stage places the river closer
to 29 ft.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 29.7 feet
this evening. The river will gradually decrease and fall below
flood stage on Saturday.
- Flood stage is 22.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
